mainTitle: 📜 Legal Analysis: Legal Framework of Violations
mainDescription: Complete legal framework — This article presents the detailed legal analysis of all violations committed against the user WazzimaGiygg (Pedro Henrique Cardona Peres), based on Brazilian legislation (LGPD, Marco Civil da Internet, Penal Code) and the Universal Code of Conduct (UCoC) of the Wikimedia Foundation.
section1Title: 1. Introduction: The Legal Dimension of the Case
section1Text1: The WazzimaGiygg case is not merely an ethical or administrative violation — it is a set of civil and criminal offenses duly defined in Brazilian legislation. The legal analysis reveals that the actions of Lusophone Wikipedia administrators and checkusers constitute multiple infractions against the Penal Code, the General Data Protection Law (LGPD) and the Marco Civil da Internet.
objective2: • Frame each act in the corresponding legal provision
objective3: • Document the legal consequences of each violation
objective4: • Establish the civil and criminal liability of the agents
warningGravityText: The case involves multiple crimes with penalties totaling up to 8 years of imprisonment, in addition to multi-million dollar fines under the LGPD and compensation for moral damages. Liability is individual and joint of the agents involved.
section2Title: 2. Violations of the Brazilian Penal Code
sub2_1Text1: Legal provision: "To slander someone, falsely imputing to them an act defined as a crime."
sub2_1Text2: Violating conduct: Chronus falsely imputed to the user the crime of threat (Art. 147 of the Penal Code) without presenting any evidence of the allegedly sent emails.

caluniaTable.description: Crime of threat (Art. 147 of Penal Code)
Detention of 6 months to 2 years + fine

caluniaWarningText: The false imputation of the crime of threat without presentation of evidence constitutes consummated slander. The penalty is detention of 6 months to 2 years, plus a fine. The fact that the accusation was made publicly on a global platform aggravates the penalty.
sub2_2Text1: Legal provision: "To defame someone, imputing to them an offensive fact to their reputation."
sub2_2Text2: Violating conduct: Public attribution of an offensive fact to the user's reputation (criminal accusation), exposing them as a "criminal" before the community.
difamacaoList: Penalty: Detention of 3 months to 1 year + fine
Aggravating factor: Disclosure on a global platform with millions of users
sub2_3Text1: Legal provision: "To injure someone, offending their dignity or decorum."
sub2_3Text2: Violating conduct: Use of offensive and humiliating terms against the user, such as "lazy puppet", "guy" and other expressions that attack their dignity.
injuriaList: Offense: Attacks on the user's dignity and honor
Penalty: Detention of 1 to 6 months or fine
Aggravating factor: Racial injury? - term "puppet" with pejorative connotation
sub2_4Text1: Legal provision: "To stalk someone, repeatedly and by any means, threatening their physical or psychological integrity."
sub2_4Text2: Violating conduct: Repeated stalking by Chronus, monitoring the user's life outside the platform (social media, forums, photographs), with public confession of wikihounding.

stalkingTable.description: Imprisonment of 6 months to 2 years (+1/3 for crimes on the internet)

stalkingWarningText: The repeated stalking, with monitoring across multiple platforms and public exposure, constitutes aggravated stalking (crime committed via the internet). The penalty is imprisonment of 6 months to 2 years, increased by 1/3 for being committed via the internet.
sub2_5Text1: Legal provision: "To invade someone else's computer device, connected or not to a computer network."
sub2_5Text2: Violating conduct: Use of scripts to capture physical hardware identifiers (IMEI and MAC Address) and collection of photo metadata (exif) without user authorization.
invasaoList: Means: Device fingerprinting, IMEI/MAC collection, exif extraction
Aggravating factor: Violation of data retention policy (logs > 90 days)
invasaoNoteText: The collection of physical hardware identifiers (IMEI and MAC Address) and the extraction of photograph metadata (exif) without authorization constitute computer device intrusion. The penalty is imprisonment of 1 to 4 years. Access to IP logs older than 90 days (violated retention policy) aggravates the crime.
sub2_6Text1: Legal provision: "For 3 (three) or more people to associate for the specific purpose of committing crimes."
sub2_6Text2: Violating conduct: Chronus, Edmond Dantès and Little Sunshine acted in coordination to build a false narrative, justify blocks without due process and prevent the user's defense.
associacaoWarningText: The systematic coordination between the three agents to neutralize the user, with division of roles and coordinated action, constitutes criminal association. The penalty is imprisonment of 1 to 3 years.
sub2_7Text1: Legal provision: "To cause the initiation of a police investigation, judicial proceeding, administrative investigation, civil inquiry or administrative impropriety action against someone, imputing to them a crime that they know they are innocent of."
sub2_7Text2: Violating conduct: Chronus falsely imputed the crime of threat; Little Sunshine, by saying "maybe now it's feasible", caused the continuation of the investigation against an innocent person.
denunciacaoList: Aggravating factor: Administrative investigation that resulted in global block
denunciacaoNoteText: By causing the administrative investigation that resulted in the user's block, imputing a crime they knew they were innocent of, Chronus and Little Sunshine constituted malicious denunciation. The penalty is imprisonment of 2 to 8 years.
section3Title: 3. Violations of the General Data Protection Law (LGPD)
sub3_1Text1: Legal provision: "Personal data processing activities must observe good faith and the following principles: I - purpose; II - adequacy; III - necessity; IV - free access; V - data quality; VI - transparency; VII - security; VIII - prevention; IX - non-discrimination; X - accountability and transparency."

lgpdPrincipiosTable.violation: Data processing with intent to persecute, not protect
Deviation of purpose - data used for persecution
Lack of transparency in data processing
Violated by public exposure of personal data
lgpdPrincipiosTable.evidence: Doxxing of civil name in public logs

sub3_2Text1: Legal provision: "Personal data processing may only be carried out in the following hypotheses: I - upon the consent of the data subject; II - for compliance with a legal or regulatory obligation; III - by the public administration; IV - for the conduct of studies by a research body; V - when necessary for the execution of a contract; VI - for the regular exercise of rights in a proceeding; VII - for the protection of life or physical safety; VIII - for health protection; IX - when necessary to meet the legitimate interests of the controller or a third party; X - for credit protection."
lgpdHipoteseList: Lack of consent: The user did not authorize the processing of their personal data.
Deviation of purpose: The processing does not fit any legal hypothesis.
Lack of legitimate interest: The controller's legitimate interest does not justify vexatious public exposure.
sub3_3Title: 3.3 Art. 20 - Right to Review Automated Decisions
sub3_3Text1: Legal provision: "The data subject has the right to request a review of decisions made solely based on automated processing of personal data that affect their interests."
lgpdRevisaoList: Violation: Automatic blocks based on device fingerprinting without a human channel for contestation.
Consequence: The user did not have the opportunity to contest the automated decision.
Harm: Global block applied without human review.
sub3_4Text1: Legal provision: "The controller or operator who, due to the exercise of personal data processing activities, causes property, moral, individual or collective damage to others, in violation of personal data protection legislation, is obliged to repair it."
lgpdResponsabilidadeList: Moral damage: Public exposure as a "criminal", linking the real name in public logs.
SEO damage: Real name permanently associated with false accusations in search engines.
Professional damage: Harm to career and professional reputation.
Liability: Controller (Wikimedia Foundation) and operators (administrators) are jointly and severally liable.
lgpdMultaText: The LGPD provides for fines of up to R$ 50 million per violation, in addition to compensation for moral and material damages. The public exposure of personal data, deviation of purpose and lack of consent constitute serious violations with high penalty potential.
sub3_5Text1: Legal provision: "Processing agents must adopt security, technical and administrative measures capable of protecting personal data from unauthorized access and from accidental or unlawful situations of destruction, loss, alteration, communication or any form of inadequate or unlawful processing."
lgpdSegurancaList: Violation: Access to IP logs older than 90 days (violation of retention policy).
Consequence: Improper exposure of personal data in public logs.
Aggravating factor: Absence of security measures to protect the victim's data.
section4Title: 4. Violations of the Marco Civil da Internet (Law 12.965/2014)
sub4_1Title: 4.1 Art. 7, II - Inviolability and Secrecy of Communications
sub4_1Text1: Legal provision: "Internet access is essential to the exercise of citizenship, and the user is assured of the following rights: II - inviolability and secrecy of the flow of their communications over the internet."
marcoSigiloList: Violation: Public disclosure that the user allegedly sent "emails with threats".
Consequence: Violation of the secrecy of private communications.
Aggravating factor: The accusation was never proven, but was publicly disclosed.
sub4_2Title: 4.2 Art. 7, IX - No Undue Suspension of Connection
sub4_2Text1: Legal provision: "Internet access is essential to the exercise of citizenship, and the user is assured of the following rights: IX - no undue suspension of their connection."
marcoSuspensaoList: Violation: Global block applied without due process and without conclusive evidence.
Consequence: Undue suspension of the user's access to the platform.
Aggravating factor: Block in 4 minutes, without adversarial proceedings.
sub4_3Title: 4.3 Art. 10 - Storage and Protection of Records
sub4_3Text1: Legal provision: "The storage and availability of connection and internet application access records referred to in this Law, as well as personal data and the content of private communications, must attend to the preservation of intimacy, private life, honor and image of the parties directly or indirectly involved."
marcoRegistrosList: Violation: CheckUser logs linking real name to nickname were made publicly available.
Consequence: Violation of the user's intimacy, private life, honor and image.
Aggravating factor: Permanent exposure in indexable public logs.
sub4_4Text1: Legal provision: "The internet application provider may only be held civilly liable for damages arising from content generated by third parties if, after a specific court order, it does not take the necessary measures to, within the scope and technical limits of its service, make the content identified as infringing unavailable."
marcoResponsabilidadeList: Liability of the Wikimedia Foundation: May be held subsidiarily liable if, after extrajudicial notification, it does not remove the defamatory content.
STF 2025 Interpretation: Platform liability has been expanded, requiring immediate removal of defamatory content even without a court order.
Consequence: The Wikimedia Foundation may be held liable for maintaining the defamatory content.

danosList: SEO damage: The doxxing log appears as the second global result on Google for the name "Pedro Henrique Cardona Peres".
Moral damage: Public exposure as a "criminal", association with false accusations.
Professional damage: Harm to career and professional reputation.
Psychological damage: Anxiety, stress, sensation of permanent persecution.
Image damage: Permanent association with false accusations in search engines.
Social damage: Isolation from the community they actively contributed to.
reparacaoList: Data removal: LGPD take-down of all personal data.
Compensation for moral damages: Financial compensation for suffering and reputational damage.
Reintegration: Reversal of the block and reintegration into the community.
De-indexation: Removal of search results on Google.
Public retraction: Official acknowledgment of the violations.
Structural reform: Governance changes to prevent new abuses.
recomendacoesList: Criminal Action: Filing of action against Chronus, Edmond Dantès, Little Sunshine and Johannesn89 for slander, malicious denunciation, criminal association, stalking and device intrusion.
Civil Action for Moral Damages: Claim for compensation for the permanent SEO Damage and for the vexatious public exposure.
Extrajudicial Notification: Sending notification to the Wikimedia Foundation for removal of defamatory content (Art. 19 of Marco Civil).
Notification to ANPD: Formal complaint to the National Data Protection Authority about LGPD violations.
Notification to the Public Prosecutor's Office: Criminal and civil complaint to the MP for violations of Brazilian legislation.
De-indexation Request: Request to Google for removal of search results (right to be forgotten).
Action in Federal Court: Jurisdiction of the Federal Court as it involves a global platform headquartered abroad.
section10Title: 10. Conclusion: The Legal Dimension of the Violations
finalText1: The WazzimaGiygg case involves multiple offenses that constitute crimes against honor, against personal liberty, against digital assets and data protection violations. Liability is individual and joint of the agents involved, with penalties totaling up to 8 years of imprisonment.
finalText2: LGPD violations may result in fines of up to R$ 50 million, in addition to compensation for moral and material damages. The Wikimedia Foundation has subsidiary liability for failing to remove defamatory content after notification.
finalText3: The legal dimension of the case transcends the scope of Wikipedia and reaches Brazilian digital law. This case may become a precedent for holding digital platforms accountable for abuses of power by their administrators.
